english.title: Registered person fail to comply with Mental Capacity Act 2005 in providing care to person unable to give consent
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[service provider]_
(B)_[registered manager]_

in respect of a regulated activity, namely **(..SPECIFY ACTIVITY..), provided care and treatment to **(..SPECIFY SERVICE USER..), a service user who was 16 or over and was unable to give consent to care and treatment because

(C)_[he]_
(D)_[she]_

lacked the capacity to do so , and, in doing so, failed to act in accordance with the Mental Capacity Act 2005 in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 11, 22(1)(a) and 23(4) of the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
being the service provider or registered manager in respect of a registered activity
provided care and treatment to a service user
who was 16 or over and was unable to give consent to care and treatment
because he or she lacked the capacity to do so
and, in doing so, failed to act in accordance with the Mental Capacity Act 2005

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 8(1) and (2) provides that a registered person must comply with regulations 9 to 20A in carrying on a regulated activity, unless the thing to be done has by another registered person in relation to the regulated activity concerned.
(ii) As per regulation 22(4), it is a defence for a registered person to prove that they took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to prevent the breach.
